mainTopic: רבי אלעזר's teachings on wives, land and blessing; business versus farming; רב פפא's practical advice; and stories of difficult wives
overview: This amud opens by finishing an earlier teaching: whoever lends money to a poor person in his time of need is promised that ה׳ will answer him. The גמרא then gives a סימן, a list of keywords for a series of teachings from רבי אלעזר. A man without a wife or without land is not a complete 'אדם'. A wife is an 'עזר' if her husband is worthy and an opponent if he is not. אליהו shows רבי יוסי how a wife helps: she turns raw wheat and flax into bread and clothing. Further teachings cover אדם finding his match in חוה, רות and נעמה being 'grafted' onto אברהם's family, and the world being blessed because of ישראל. Next come sayings that business earns more than farming, and רב פפא's practical advice on food, clothing, building, land, marriage and friends. The amud ends with stories about difficult wives. These include רב's wife, who always cooked the opposite of what he asked, and his son, whom he told not to lie even to fix it. Finally, רבי חייא explains why he was still kind to his wife, and his answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Lending to a poor person in his time of need
steps.stepSummary: The last line of an earlier teaching: whoever lends a סלע to a poor person when he is desperate is promised that ה׳ will answer his prayers.
steps.simpleTranslation: And someone who lends a סלע coin to a poor person at the time he is pressed for money, about him the verse says: 'Then you will call, and ה׳ will answer; you will cry out, and He will say: Here I am.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a list of praiseworthy people that began before this section. This last item is about someone who lends money to a poor person exactly when he needs it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key words are 'בשעת דחקו', at his time of pressure. The reward fits the deed: he answered the poor man's need right away, so ה׳ answers his call right away with 'Here I am.'

keyTerms.meaning: at his time of pressure or desperate need

phrases.english: And one who lends a sela to a poor person at his time of need
about him the verse says:
'Then you will call, and ה׳ will answer;
you will cry out, and He will say: Here I am.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes a list of praiseworthy people that began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Someone who lends to a poor person in his time of need is promised that ה׳ will answer him immediately.

steps.title: A memory list for רבי אלעזר's teachings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a list of keywords to help remember the series of רבי אלעזר's teachings that come next.
steps.simpleTranslation: Memory aid: Woman. And land. Helper. This. Two. The blessings. Merchants. Lowly.
steps.whatsHappening: This line is not a teaching by itself. The גמרא is setting up what comes next by giving a list of keywords, one for each of רבי אלעזר's upcoming statements.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each word stands for one of רבי אלעזר's teachings, in order. אשה is step 3 and קרקע is step 4. עזר is steps 5-8, זאת is step 9, and שתי הברכות is steps 10-11. תגרי is step 12, where craftsmen and seafarers end up on the land. פחתי is step 13, where farming is called the lowest occupation.

keyTerms.meaning: a memory aid made of keywords

steps.confusionAlert: Don't try to read the סימן as one sentence. It is just a list of keywords, each pointing to a separate teaching that comes later.

phrases.english: Memory aid: Woman. And land. Helper.
phrases.notes: Each word is a reminder of one of רבי אלעזר's teachings that follow, in order.

phrases.english: This. Two. The blessings.
Merchants. Lowly.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new section, a series of רבי אלעזר's teachings.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A list of keywords for the coming teachings of רבי אלעזר.

steps.title: A man without a wife is not a complete man
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר teaches that a man without a wife is not called 'אדם', based on the פסוק that calls male and female together 'אדם'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: Any man who has no wife is not a man, as it says: 'Male and female He created them, and He called their name אדם.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר gives his first teaching, which matches the keyword 'אשה'. He proves it from a פסוק in בראשית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק gives the name 'אדם' only to male and female together. So a man alone is missing part of what makes him a complete 'אדם'.

keyTerms.meaning: as it is said (introduces a פסוק)

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
Any man who does not have a wife
is not a man,
as it is said: 'Male and female He created them,
and He called their name Adam.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: כׇּל אָדָם שֶׁאֵין לוֹ אִשָּׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The first teaching on the memory list (אשה).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only male and female together are called 'אדם', so a man without a wife is incomplete.

steps.title: A man without land is not a complete man
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר teaches that a man without his own land is not a complete 'אדם', since the earth was given to 'בני אדם'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אלעזר said: Any man who has no land is not a man, as it says: 'The heavens are the heavens of ה׳, but the earth He gave to the children of men.'
steps.whatsHappening: This is the second teaching on the list (קרקע). It has the same pattern as the first one, with a new proof from תהלים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says the earth was given to 'בני אדם'. So owning a piece of it is part of being a complete 'אדם', and a man with no land is missing his share.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Elazar said:
Any man who does not have land
is not a man,
as it is said: 'The heavens are the heavens of ה׳,
but the earth He gave to the children of men.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: כׇּל אָדָם שֶׁאֵין לוֹ קַרְקַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The second teaching on the memory list, using the same pattern as step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The earth was given to people, so a man without land is incomplete.

steps.title: A helper or an opponent, depending on merit
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר explains the words 'עזר כנגדו': if the husband is worthy his wife helps him, and if he is not worthy she is against him.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אלעזר said: What does the verse mean, 'I will make him a helper against him'? If he is worthy, she helps him; if he is not worthy, she is against him.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the third teaching on the list (עזר). רבי אלעזר explains why the פסוק uses two words that seem to clash: 'helper' and 'against him'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'עזר' means helper, and 'כנגדו' can mean opposite or against him. רבי אלעזר says the two words describe two possible outcomes, and the husband's own merit decides which one comes true.

keyTerms.meaning: what is the meaning of what is written

phrases.english: And Rabbi Elazar said: What is the meaning of that which is written:
'I will make for him a helper opposite him'?
If he is worthy, she helps him;
if he is not worthy, she is against him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The third teaching on the memory list (עזר).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'עזר' and 'כנגדו' are two possible outcomes, and which one happens depends on the husband's merit.

steps.title: Another version: the written spelling versus how we read it
steps.stepSummary: Another version of רבי אלעזר's teaching: he bases it on the gap between how the word is spelled (allowing the reading כְּנַגְּדוֹ, striking him) and how it is read (כְּנֶגְדּוֹ, fitting for him).
steps.simpleTranslation: And some say: רבי אלעזר pointed out a contradiction. It is written in a way that can be read 'כְּנַגְּדוֹ' (striking him), yet we read it 'כְּנֶגְדּוֹ' (fitting for him). If he is worthy, she is fitting for him; if he is not worthy, she strikes him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second report of the same teaching from רבי אלעזר. In this version, his source is the spelling of the word, not the meaning of the two words together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here 'כְּנֶגְדּוֹ', the way we read it, is the good outcome: a partner suited to him. The spelling allows the reading 'כְּנַגְּדוֹ', from 'striking', which is the bad outcome. The bad side is also stronger in this version: she does not just stand against him, she actively strikes at him.

keyTerms.meaning: it is written one way, and we read it another way

steps.confusionAlert: Notice that 'כנגדו' changes roles. In the first version it was the bad outcome (against him). In this version, read 'כְּנֶגְדּוֹ', it is the good outcome (fitting for him).

phrases.english: And some say:
Rabbi Elazar pointed out a contradiction:
It is written 'striking him', and we read it 'fitting for him'.
phrases.notes: The letters of the word allow the reading 'כְּנַגְּדוֹ', from a word for striking, but we pronounce it 'כְּנֶגְדּוֹ'.

phrases.english: If he is worthy, she is fitting for him;
if he is not worthy, she strikes him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different version of the teaching in step 5, based on the spelling of the word.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Based on spelling versus reading: a worthy husband gets a partner suited to him, and an unworthy one gets a wife who strikes at him.

steps.title: רבי יוסי asks אליהו how a wife helps
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי meets אליהו הנביא and asks him how a wife is a 'helper' to her husband, as the פסוק says.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי met אליהו. He said to him: It is written, 'I will make him a helper.' In what way does a woman help a man?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story that continues the topic of 'עזר'. רבי יוסי asks אליהו what practical help a wife gives, and this sets up אליהו's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now we learned that a wife can be a helper. רבי יוסי wants to know what that help actually looks like in daily life.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei met Elijah
and said to him: It is written: 'I will make him a helper.'
In what way does a woman help a man?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Picks up the word 'עזר' from step 5 and asks what the help actually is.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: In what practical way is a wife a helper to her husband?

steps.title: אליהו: she turns raw materials into food and clothing
steps.stepSummary: אליהו answers that a husband brings home raw wheat and flax, and his wife turns them into bread and clothing. So she lights up his eyes and stands him on his feet.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: A man brings home wheat. Does he chew raw wheat? He brings flax. Does he wear raw flax? Isn't she the one who lights up his eyes and stands him on his feet?!
steps.whatsHappening: אליהו answers רבי יוסי's question with examples from everyday life. The husband brings raw materials, and the wife makes them usable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Raw wheat and raw flax are useless as they are. The wife's work turns them into food and clothing. That is why 'עזר' means she gives him what he needs to function, lighting up his eyes and keeping him on his feet.
steps.whatToRemember: A wife is called 'עזר' because she turns what her husband brings home into real food and clothing, giving him life and strength.

phrases.english: He said to him:
A man brings wheat. Does he chew raw wheat?
He brings flax. Does he wear raw flax?
Is she not found to light up his eyes
and stand him on his feet?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי יוסי's question from step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A wife turns raw wheat and flax into bread and clothing, giving her husband life and strength.

steps.title: אדם was only settled once he found חוה
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר explains the words 'זאת הפעם' to mean that אדם found no fitting partner among the animals, and his mind was only at ease with חוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אלעזר said: What does the פסוק mean, 'This time, bone of my bones and flesh of my flesh'? It teaches that אדם had relations with every animal and beast, and his mind was not settled until he came to חוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another teaching of רבי אלעזר, explaining what אדם meant when he first saw חוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'הפעם' (this time) suggests there were earlier tries that did not work. רבי אלעזר says those tries were with the animals. Only with חוה, who was made from his own body, did אדם feel complete.

keyTerms.meaning: His mind was settled and at ease

phrases.english: And Rabbi Elazar said:
What is the meaning of that which is written:
"This time, bone of my bones
and flesh of my flesh" —
this teaches that Adam had relations
with every domestic animal and wild beast,
and his mind was not settled
until he came to Chava.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the chain of רבי אלעזר's teachings about a wife and her husband.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אדם found no fitting partner until חוה; the word 'הפעם' shows the earlier attempts failed.

steps.title: Two good shoots grafted onto אברהם
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר reads 'ונברכו' in the blessing to אברהם as 'grafting', a hint to רות and נעמה, who would join his family.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אלעזר said: What does the פסוק mean, 'And in you shall all the families of the earth be blessed'? הקדוש ברוך הוא said to אברהם: I have two good shoots to graft onto you: רות the Moabite and נעמה the Ammonite.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר explains a word in the blessing to אברהם as a hint to two women from other nations who would join his family.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He links 'ונברכו' (be blessed) to 'להבריך' (to graft a branch onto a tree). רות and נעמה came from מואב and עמון, but they were 'grafted' onto אברהם's family tree and became part of it.

keyTerms.meaning: And they shall be blessed (read here as related to grafting)
To graft a branch onto a tree

phrases.english: And Rabbi Elazar said: What is the meaning of that which is written:
"And in you shall be blessed
all the families of the earth"?

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְאַבְרָהָם:
phrases.english: The Holy One, Blessed be He, said to Avraham:
Two good shoots
I have to graft onto you:
phrases.notes: A wordplay: 'ונברכו' sounds like 'להבריך', planting a branch so it grows from the tree.

phrases.english: Ruth the Moabite and Naamah the Ammonite.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The next teaching on the memory list (שתי הברכות), on a different פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'ונברכו' hints at grafting רות and נעמה onto אברהם's family.

steps.title: The whole world is blessed because of Israel
steps.stepSummary: From the words 'כל משפחות האדמה' and 'כל גויי הארץ' the גמרא teaches that even landowners and even far-off sea traders are blessed only because of ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'All the families of the earth': even families who live on their own land are blessed only because of ישראל. 'All the nations of the earth': even ships that travel from Galia to Aspamia are blessed only because of ישראל.
steps.whatsHappening: The teaching goes on to read two phrases from the blessings to אברהם as saying that all the world's success comes through ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'האדמה' (the land) is read as people settled on land, and 'כל גויי הארץ' is stretched to include even sea traders far away. Both groups, on land and at sea, get their blessing because of ישראל.

phrases.english: "All the families of the earth" —
even families who live on the land
are blessed only because of Israel.
"All the nations of the earth" —
even ships that travel from Galia to Aspamia
are blessed only because of Israel.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֹּל מִשְׁפְּחוֹת הָאֲדָמָה — אֲפִילּוּ מִשְׁפָּחוֹת הַדָּרוֹת בָּאֲדָמָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues expounding the blessing to אברהם from the previous step.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Everyone, on land and at sea, is blessed only because of ישראל.

steps.title: In the future all craftsmen will work the land
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר teaches from a פסוק in יחזקאל that in the future all craftsmen will leave their trades and work the land.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אלעזר said: In the future all craftsmen will stand on the land, as it says: 'And they will come down from their ships, all who hold the oar, the sailors, all the captains of the sea; they will stand on the land.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching of רבי אלעזר that begins a topic about working the land.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק describes sailors leaving their ships to stand on land. רבי אלעזר takes the sailors as an example of all people with trades, who will one day turn to farming.

keyTerms.meaning: They are destined, in the future

phrases.english: And Rabbi Elazar said:
All craftsmen are destined
to stand upon the land,
as it is stated: "And they will come down from their ships,
all who hold the oar, the sailors,
all the captains of the sea;
upon the land they will stand."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: עֲתִידִים כׇּל בַּעֲלֵי אוּמָּנִיּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic in the chain of רבי אלעזר's teachings: working the land.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the future, all craftsmen will turn to working the land.

steps.title: No occupation is lower than farming
steps.stepSummary: Using the same פסוק, רבי אלעזר teaches that working the land is the lowest of all occupations, because the sailors 'come down' to it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אלעזר said: There is no occupation lower than working the land, as it says: 'And they will come down.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר uses the same פסוק to make a second point, this time about how low farming ranks.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sailors move from ships to land, and the פסוק calls this 'coming down'. So moving to farming is a step down, even from the hard life of a sailor.
steps.confusionAlert: Earlier (step 4) רבי אלעזר said a man without land is not a complete 'אדם'. Here he says farming is the lowest way to earn a living. These are two different points: owning land, and land as a job for making money.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Elazar said:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין לְךָ אוּמָּנוּת פְּחוּתָה מִן הַקַּרְקַע,
phrases.english: There is no occupation lower than working the land,
as it is stated: "And they will come down."
phrases.notes: Same פסוק as before. Going from the ships to the land is called going 'down'.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: אֵין לְךָ אוּמָּנוּת פְּחוּתָה מִן הַקַּרְקַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a second lesson from the same פסוק in יחזקאל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Farming is the lowest of all occupations.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר speaks to a plowed field
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר sees a field plowed across its width and tells it that even with extra plowing, business is better than farming it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר saw a field that had been plowed across its width. He said to it: Even if they plow you along your length too, doing business is better than you.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a short story about רבי אלעזר that backs up his teaching that farming is a weak way to make a living.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Plowing a second time, lengthwise, would improve the field and its harvest. Still, רבי אלעזר says that even a well-worked field earns less than trading in goods.

keyTerms.meaning: Trading in business, buying and selling goods

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar saw a certain field
that had been plowed across its width.
He said to it:
Even if they plow you along your length —
trading in business is better than you.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A story that illustrates רבי אלעזר's statement that farming is lowly.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even a well-worked field earns less than business.

steps.title: רב speaks to the swaying grain
steps.stepSummary: רב walks among swaying stalks of grain and tells them that, however nicely they sway, business is better than farming.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב went in among the stalks of grain and saw them swaying. He said to them: If you want to sway, go ahead and sway. Doing business is better than you.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a similar story about רב, making the same point as רבי אלעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Swaying grain looks like a rich, healthy crop. רב is saying that even a crop that looks so good does not match the profit of business.

phrases.english: Rav went in among the stalks of grain,
and saw them swaying.
He said to them:
If you want to sway, go ahead and sway.
Trading in business is better than you.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel story with the same closing line as רבי אלעזר's.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even a fine-looking crop earns less than business.

steps.title: רבא compares money in business and money in land
steps.stepSummary: רבא says a hundred זוז in business gives meat and wine every day, while a hundred זוז in land gives only salt and vegetables, plus hardship and quarrels.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: A hundred זוז in business means meat and wine every day. A hundred זוז in land means salt and vegetables. And not only that, the land makes him sleep on the ground and brings quarrels upon him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא closes the topic with a clear comparison that explains why business is better than farming.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the same hundred זוז, business brings a rich living while land brings a poor one. רבא then adds two more problems with land: the owner must sleep in the field to guard it, and it causes fights with others.

keyTerms.meaning: Salt and vegetables, a poor man's meal

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אלעזר, רב and רבא all agree: as a way of making a living, business brings far more than farming, and farming also brings hardship and fights.

phrases.english: Rava said:
A hundred zuz in business —
meat and wine every day;
a hundred zuz in land —
salt and vegetables.
And not only that, but
it makes him lie down on the ground,
phrases.notes: He has to sleep out in the field at night to guard his crops.

phrases.english: and it brings quarrels upon him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out in numbers the lesson of the two stories before it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Money in business brings a rich living; money in land brings a poor living, hardship and quarrels.

steps.title: Grow your own food rather than buy it
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא advises sowing your own produce rather than buying it, because home-grown produce carries a ברכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: Sow your own food and do not buy it. Even if the cost comes out the same, what you grow yourself is blessed.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא begins a list of short practical rules. The first rule is to grow your own produce instead of buying it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On paper, growing and buying may cost the same. רב פפא adds something money cannot measure: what you grow yourself gets a ברכה.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
Sow, and do not buy.

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּכִי הֲדָדֵי נִינְהוּ,
phrases.english: Even though they are equal to each other,
phrases.notes: He means the cost of growing it and the cost of buying it come out about the same.

phrases.english: these are blessed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: זְרַע וְלָא תִּזְבֹּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the series of sayings about earning a living. It adds a ברכה-based reason to grow your own food.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Grow your own produce rather than buy it, because home-grown produce is blessed.

steps.title: Buy cloth goods rather than weave them, except a cloak
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא advises buying woven goods rather than making them. The גמרא limits this to mats, since a cloak bought ready-made may not fit well.
steps.simpleTranslation: Buy, and do not weave. This applies only to mats. A cloak you buy may not suit you, so make that one yourself.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא gives the opposite advice for cloth: buy it, don't weave it. The גמרא then limits this rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For food, home-grown is better. For woven goods, buying is better. The גמרא narrows that rule to items like mats. A bought cloak may not turn out right for the person wearing it, so making your own is better.

phrases.english: Buy, and do not weave.
This applies to mats,
but a cloak —
it may not turn out right for him.

steps.triggerLanguage: זַבֵּין וְלָא תִּיזּוֹל. הָנֵי מִילֵּי בִּיסְתַּרְקֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The opposite rule for cloth goods, followed by the גמרא's limit on that rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Buy woven items like mats rather than weave them, but make your own cloak so it fits you.

steps.title: Patch a house rather than rebuild it
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא advises doing the smallest repair possible, because anyone who gets involved in building becomes poor.
steps.simpleTranslation: Close up the hole and do not plaster. Plaster and do not rebuild. Anyone who gets busy with construction becomes poor.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא advises keeping house repairs as small as possible. He gives the reason: building makes a person poor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule moves step by step. A simple patch is better than a plaster job, and a plaster job is better than knocking the wall down and rebuilding. Building projects grow and eat up money, so the smallest fix is the wisest one.

phrases.english: Close up, and do not plaster.
phrases.notes: He's talking about a hole or crack in your house. Just patch it.

phrases.english: Plaster, and do not build.
For anyone who busies himself with building
becomes poor.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: More of רב פפא's money advice, now about house repairs.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Make the smallest repair possible, because building projects make a person poor.

steps.title: Rush for land, take your time with marriage, and choose a friend wisely
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא advises hurrying to buy land but marrying slowly. He also says to marry a little below your social level and to choose a friend a little above it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Hurry to buy land. Take your time to marry a woman. Go down a step to marry a woman. Go up a step to choose a close friend.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא ends his list with advice on timing and on choosing people. He covers buying land, marrying, and picking a close friend.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A good piece of land can be gone quickly, so buy it fast. A wife is for life, so don't rush. A wife from a slightly lower level will not look down on you. A friend from a slightly higher level lifts you up.

keyTerms.meaning: Close friend (best man at a wedding)

steps.whatToRemember: רב פפא's rules: grow food rather than buy it; buy mats rather than weave them, but make your own cloak; patch rather than rebuild; hurry for land, go slowly with marriage; marry a step down, befriend a step up.

phrases.english: Jump to buy land,
be slow to marry a woman.
Go down a step to marry a woman.
Go up a step to choose a close friend.

steps.triggerLanguage: קְפוֹץ זְבֹין אַרְעָא, מְתוֹן נְסֵיב אִיתְּתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רב פפא's list of practical advice.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Hurry to buy land, marry slowly, marry a step down, and choose a friend a step up.

steps.title: Calamity comes to the world because of ישראל
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר בר אבינא teaches that disasters come to the world only so that ישראל will learn a lesson. He proves it from two פסוקים in צפניה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר בר אבינא said: Calamity comes to the world only because of ישראל. The פסוק says, 'I cut off nations... I made their streets waste,' and right after that it says, 'I said, surely you will fear Me, you will accept correction.'
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching begins. רבי אלעזר בר אבינא teaches that when disaster hits other nations, the real purpose is to send a message to ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first פסוק describes nations being destroyed. The very next פסוק speaks to ישראל: 'surely you will fear Me.' Putting the two together shows that the nations were punished so ישראל would see it and do תשובה.

keyTerms.meaning: Because of, for the sake of

steps.whyThisMatters: This changes how a Jew should look at world disasters. They are a personal wake-up call, not something happening only to other people.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar bar Avina said:
Calamity does not come to the world
except because of Israel,
as it says:
"I cut off nations, their corners are desolate,
I made their streets waste,"
and it is written:
"I said: surely you will fear Me,
you will accept correction."
phrases.notes: צפניה 3:7, the very next פסוק. The nations were hit so that ישראל would take the lesson.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בַּר אֲבִינָא: אֵין פּוּרְעָנוּת בָּאָה לָעוֹלָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new, separate teaching. It is not connected to רב פפא's advice.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Calamity comes to the world only so that ישראל will learn and improve.

steps.title: רבי חייא blesses רב to be saved from something worse than death
steps.stepSummary: When רב leaves רבי חייא, רבי חייא blesses him to be saved from something harsher than death.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב was taking leave of רבי חייא. רבי חייא said to him: May the Merciful One save you from something harsher than death.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a story about wives. רבי חייא gives רב a puzzling blessing, and this sets up the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The blessing is worded like a riddle. רבי חייא doesn't say what this 'something harsher than death' is. That makes רב, and us, curious.

phrases.english: Rav was taking leave of Rabbi Ḥiyya,
he said to him:
phrases.notes: It's רבי חייא speaking to רב.

phrases.english: May the Merciful One save you
from something harsher than death.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new story section about wives.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי חייא blesses רב to be spared from something worse than death.

steps.title: Is anything worse than death?
steps.stepSummary: רב wonders what could possibly be harsher than death.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is there really anything harsher than death?
steps.whatsHappening: רב is puzzled by the blessing and asks what could be worse than death. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Death seems like the worst thing that can happen to a person. So רב needs to find out what רבי חייא had in mind.

phrases.english: And is there something harsher than death?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A question about the wording of רבי חייא's blessing.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What could possibly be harsher than death?

steps.title: רב finds the פסוק: a bad wife is more bitter than death
steps.stepSummary: רב searches and finds a פסוק in קהלת that calls a certain woman more bitter than death.
steps.simpleTranslation: He went out, looked carefully, and found: 'And I find more bitter than death the woman...'
steps.whatsHappening: רב answers his own question by finding a פסוק. It shows that רבי חייא was talking about a bad wife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in קהלת says outright that a certain kind of woman is 'more bitter than death.' So רבי חייא's blessing meant: may you be spared a difficult wife.

phrases.english: He went out, examined, and found:
"And I find more bitter than death
the woman, etc."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of what is harsher than death.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A bad wife is harsher than death, as the פסוק in קהלת says.

steps.title: רב's wife always made the opposite of what he asked
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that רב himself had a difficult wife. Whatever dish he asked for, she made the other one.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב's wife used to aggravate him. When he told her, 'Make me lentils,' she made him peas. When he asked for peas, she made him lentils.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows how רבי חייא's blessing connected to real life. רב's own wife kept doing the opposite of what he asked.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a concrete example of the 'bitter' wife from the פסוק. The problem was not one big fight but steady, everyday contrariness. The story continues in the next lines.

phrases.aramaic: רַב הֲוָה קָא מְצַעֲרָא לֵיהּ דְּבֵיתְהוּ,
phrases.english: Rav's wife used to aggravate him.
When he said to her, "Make me lentils,"
she made him peas.
"Peas" — she made him lentils.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב הֲוָה קָא מְצַעֲרָא לֵיהּ דְּבֵיתְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a real-life example of the bad wife the פסוק describes, in רב's own home.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב's wife always did the opposite of what he asked, showing the difficult wife that רבי חייא's blessing warned about.

steps.title: רב's son flips the requests
steps.stepSummary: When רב's son חייא grew up, he reversed רב's requests when passing them to his mother.
steps.simpleTranslation: When חייא, his son, grew up, he would reverse the requests for her.
steps.whatsHappening: The story of רב's difficult wife continues. Their son חייא now delivers רב's requests, and he says the opposite of what רב asked.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 25 said she always made the opposite of what רב asked. If חייא tells her the opposite, her habit of doing the opposite makes her cook exactly what רב wanted.

phrases.english: When Ḥiyya, his son, grew up,
he would reverse it for her.
phrases.notes: He would pass along the opposite of what רב asked. Since she always does the opposite, רב ends up getting what he wanted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story of רב's wife from step 25.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חייא reversed his father's requests so his mother would make what רב wanted.

steps.title: רב thinks his wife has improved
steps.stepSummary: רב tells his son that his mother has gotten better.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Your mother has improved for you!
steps.whatsHappening: רב notices that he is suddenly getting the food he asks for. He thinks his wife has changed, and he says so to his son. This sets up the son's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב does not know about the trick. He gives the credit to his wife, and that sets up the son's surprising answer.

phrases.english: He said to him: Your mother has improved for you!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רב reacts to the result of the son's trick without knowing about it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב thinks his wife has improved.

steps.title: The son reveals his trick
steps.stepSummary: חייא tells רב that the change happened because he reverses the requests.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: It is I who reverse it for her.
steps.whatsHappening: The son explains that his mother has not changed. He is the one flipping the requests.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This corrects רב's assumption from step 27. The good result came from the son's cleverness, not from any change in the mother.

phrases.english: He said to him: It is I
who reverses it for her.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אֲנָא הוּא דְּקָא אָפֵיכְנָא לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers and corrects רב's remark in step 27.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The improvement comes from the son flipping the requests.

steps.title: רב praises his son's cleverness
steps.stepSummary: רב quotes a popular saying: your own child can teach you wisdom.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: This is what people say: The one who comes from you teaches you wisdom.
steps.whatsHappening: רב admires the idea. He quotes a well-known saying that even your child can teach you something smart.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב admits the trick is clever and works. This praise sets up his next line, where he still tells his son not to use it.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ, הַיְינוּ דְּקָא אָמְרִי אִינָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: He said to him: This is what people say:
The one who comes from you teaches you wisdom.
phrases.notes: Literally 'the one who comes out of you.' He means your own child.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רב reacts to the son's explanation.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Your own child can teach you wisdom.

steps.title: רב tells his son not to lie
steps.stepSummary: רב tells his son to stop the trick, because it means saying something false, and brings a פסוק from ירמיה.
steps.simpleTranslation: You should not do so, as it says: "They have taught their tongue to speak lies, they weary themselves to do wrong, etc."
steps.whatsHappening: Even though the trick works, רב tells his son not to do it. He supports this with a פסוק that criticizes people who train themselves to lie.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Telling the mother 'Father wants X' when he really wants Y is a lie. רב's comfort is not worth teaching his son to speak falsely, so he rejects the method even though it helps him.
steps.whatToRemember: A smart trick that makes peace at home is still not allowed if it means getting used to lying.
steps.whyThisMatters: רב gives up his own benefit so his son will not learn to lie. Honesty comes before convenience.

phrases.english: You should not do so,
as it is stated: "They have taught their tongue to speak lies,
to do wrong, etc."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After praising the trick, רב rejects it.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The son's method of flipping the requests.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It involves telling a lie in his father's name.

steps.title: רבי חייא brings gifts to his difficult wife
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא's wife gave him trouble, yet he would wrap things he found and bring them to her.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא's wife would aggravate him. When he found something, he would wrap it in his scarf and bring it to her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a similar story about another difficult wife. רבי חייא still treated his wife kindly and brought her gifts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same רבי חייא who blessed רב in step 22 to be saved from a bad wife. He also had a hard wife, but he answered her with generosity.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי חִיָּיא הֲוָה קָא מְצַעֲרָא לֵיהּ דְּבֵיתְהוּ.
phrases.english: Rabbi Chiyya's wife would aggravate him.
When he would find something,
he would wrap it in his scarf
and bring it to her.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי חִיָּיא הֲוָה קָא מְצַעֲרָא לֵיהּ דְּבֵיתְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new story on the same theme of a difficult wife.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי חייא gave gifts to his wife even though she made his life hard.

steps.title: רב asks why he is so kind to her
steps.stepSummary: רב asks רבי חייא why he brings gifts to a wife who aggravates him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said to him: But doesn't she aggravate the master?
steps.whatsHappening: רב is surprised. He asks why רבי חייא is generous to someone who treats him badly. This sets up רבי חייא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is based on simple logic: you would not expect someone to reward a person who causes him pain. The question has some challenge in it, but its main job is to get רבי חייא to explain himself.

phrases.english: Rav said to him:
But doesn't she aggravate the master?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions רבי חייא's behavior described in step 31.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רבי חייא is generous to a wife who causes him trouble.

steps.title: Wives raise our children and save us
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא answers that it is enough that wives raise our children and save us.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: It is enough for us that they raise our children and save us...
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חייא explains why he stays generous. Even a difficult wife does huge good things, like raising the children and saving her husband.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חייא looks at what his wife gives, not only at the trouble she causes. Raising the children alone deserves his thanks, and the sentence goes on to name what else they save us from.
steps.whyThisMatters: It teaches you to value a spouse for the good they bring, even when things are hard.

phrases.english: He said to him: It is enough for us
that they raise our children,
and save us

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב's question in step 32.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Wives deserve thanks because they raise the children and save their husbands.
